Global Broadcast: Once ignition occurs, contents of the workspace are broadcast via long-range projections back to all specialized modules, implementing access consciousness—the reportable, actionable availability of information across the brain (Rosenbloom et al., 13 Jun 2025, VanRullen et al., 2020).
 Recurrent Processing: Both ignition and sustained workspace activity are maintained by recurrent local and global feedback loops, supporting cycling and integration of information (Rosenbloom et al., 13 Jun 2025).
 Unitary Access: At any instant, only a single or small set of representations dominate the workspace, accounting for the unitarity of conscious experience (Kavi et al., 2024). The global workspace controller facilitates ignition, conflict resolution, broadcast, re-entry updates, and dynamic personality evolution, yielding emergent conscious-like properties in digital twins and LLM-based social agents (Ye et al., 4 Jun 2025, Goldstein et al., 2024). [...] The Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT) is a leading neuroscientific theory of consciousness proposing that conscious access arises from the dynamic competition, ignition, and global broadcasting of information among distributed, specialized brain modules, mediated by a recurrent integrative workspace. GNWT postulates that a relatively sparse population of high-connectivity workspace neurons in prefrontal and parietal regions act as a bottleneck and relay, enabling transient, discrete contents to become the unitary focus of conscious experience while integrating perception, memory, attention, and action selection. results.title: Global Workspace Theory and the Missing Architecture of AI Cognition
results.content:
Micheal Lanham

## Executive Summary

Global Workspace Theory (GWT) posits that conscious cognition functions as a capacity-limited “broadcast” mechanism, allowing information selected by attention to become globally available to a “society” of specialized, semi-independent processes. While modern AI agents utilize Large Language Model (LLM) loops and message-passing protocols, they generally lack a dedicated architecture for continuous “shared awareness.” By synthesizing GWT with the biological “ignition” model and classical “blackboard” AI systems, a new architectural layer for AI is proposed. This Global Workspace (GW) layer would implement shared state, attention-based routing, and broadcast protocols to enable more flexible, coordinated, and coherent multi-step problem solving. [...] ## Limitations of Current Agentic AI Architectures

Modern AI agents often approximate workspace-like behaviors but lack the dedicated architectural layer required for true global broadcast dynamics.

results.content:
# Conscious Processing in Global Neuronal Workspace

This document reviews the global neuronal workspace (GNW) hypothesis, which proposes that conscious processing involves the ignition and sustained recurrent activity of a distributed network in the brain. The key tenets of the GNW hypothesis are described, including that it involves the broadcasting of information from specialized processors to widely distributed excitatory neurons that can mobilize other processors. Recent neuroimaging data that support the hypothesis by contrasting conscious and non-conscious brain activity are discussed. The relationship between conscious processing, attention, and working memory within the framework of the GNW is also examined.
